pr_body:
~Service `Type=any` is meant for interactive applications whose forking model is not known ahead of time, so mainly for transient services.~

~Similar to `simple`, The service manager will consider the unit started as soon as the main service process has been forked off. However, the service will stay running as long as at least one process in the cgroup is running. There is no specific main process for the service. The exit status of the service is that of the last process in the cgroup to exit, so it will be considered to have crashed only if the last process crashed, not if any other process in the cgroup crashes.~

~Other possible names: `Type=cgroup`, `Type=simple-multiprocess`~
Closes #16805

This PR introduces `ExitType=main|cgroup` for services. Similar to how `Type` specifies the launch of a service, `ExitType` is concerned with how systemd determines that a service exited. 

- If set to `main` (the current behavior), the service manager will consider the unit stopped when the main process exits.

- The `cgroup` exit type is meant for applications whose forking model is not known ahead of time and which might not have a specific main process. The service will stay running as long as at least one process in the cgroup is running. The exit status of the service is that of the last process in the cgroup to exit. This is intended for transient or automatically generated services, such as graphical applications inside of a desktop environment.

Motivation for this is #16805 . `xdg-autostart-generator` was amended to use `ExitType=cgroup`, which fixes a [bug](https://bugs.kde.org/show_bug.cgi?id=433299) with some generated autostart app services that forked not launching (systemd killed the entire cgroup after the main process exited)

Can you explain what the difference is (and in particular is better) than Type=forking + RemainAfterExit=yes

> Can you explain what the difference is (and in particular is better) than Type=forking + RemainAfterExit=yes

(didn't know you can mix those, nice)

> Can you explain what the difference is (and in particular is better) than Type=forking + RemainAfterExit=yes
- single process application (or initial process that outlives its children)
  +  with `Type=forking` `RemainAfterExit=true`  
  `activating(start)` => `active(exited)`
  +  with `Type=cgroup`  / `any`
  `active(running)` => `inactive`

- application that forks and initial process dies at some point
  + with `Type=forking` `RemainAfterExit=true` 
  `activating(start)` =initial process exits=> `active(running)`  =last process exits=> `active (exited)`
  +  with `Type=cgroup`    / `any`
  `active(running)` =last process exits=> `inactive`

So the service ends up inactive instead of active after all processes exit, and reliably becomes running as soon as it should  (as discussed last summer over telegram). This means restarts can work.

Also we are able to track the exit reason of the last process and eg restart accordingly
@poettering also `Type=forking RemainAfterExit=true` needs `TimeoutStartSec=infinity` to work at all which is starting to look a bit hackish

Please drop "interactive" from the man page change: it's confusing in this context.

> Also I'm reconsidering whether to also use the behavior of `Type=exec` (only considering the unit started after `exec` succeeded) rather than `simple` as it might be more useful for applications.

Yes, that would be better. Type=simple should be considered legacy at this point.

--

I think this is quite useful, but I'm not sure if the semantics are correct. This mixes two things: when the service is considered started, and when it is considered finished. Your main goal is to specify a new behaviour for the latter, but the current approach of adding a new Type hardcodes a specific mechanism for the first property too. I think that instead of a new Type, this should be boolean property that could be set for various Types (at least simple, exec, notify, and forking would make sense). Something like AnyProcessesIsAGoodProcess=true (name TBD of course).

(So for example, I could have Type=notify + AnyProcessesIsAGoodProcess=true for a web listener which needs to do some nontrivial initialization before dependent services should be started and needs Type=notify, but after starting there is no specific main process, just a bunch of workers that come and go as necessary.)

StopType=any,main etc...

It's similar to Type= since it decides when to transition from Active to the stopping logic and having an enum instead of a boolean allows us to add more behaviours ?
Please list the new directive in test/fuzz/fuzz-unit-file/directives.service

Looks good to me. I like the new separate option a lot better. Let's merge after 248.

issue_context.title: New service `Type=any`
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
As part of moving desktop applications to be managed by systemd as transient services in KDE, while most `.desktop` apps have the parent process run for the lifetime of the application (corresponding to `Type=simple`), some apps fork and exit (corresponding to `Type=forking`). We cannot know in advance which forking model the app uses.
In addition, some apps might launch detached instances of themselves at a later time (after a double fork), expecting the detached instance to survive the initial one when it exits

**Describe the solution you'd like**
A new `Type=any` (or `Type=cgroup` ?) that considers the service running as long as at least one process in the tree is running (doesn't rely on PID files or PID guessing as there is no specific main process).
The exit status of the service is that of the last process in the cgroup, so it will be considered to have crashed only if the last process crashed, not if any other process in the cgroup crashes.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Using `Type=simple` with default `KillMode` leads to the entire application being killed as soon as the parent process exits.
Changing to `KillMode=none` means we lose graceful shutdown
Using `Type=forking` means regular non-forking apps are never considered started
comments: Reopening - unfortunately https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/18782 had to be reverted by https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/20073 to unblock the v249 release, as it was causing issues ( https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/19345 and https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/19385 ). Would be great to have a new PR that reintroduces the feature and fixes those issues as well
